decisions.reason: The 5V rail still supplies the SPS30 and ZE08 sensors, so moving the LEDs to 3.3V does not change the requirement to monitor both the 3.3V and 5V rails.

This Requirement already has a complete message-444 MODIFY recording the 3.3V LED supply, direct ESP32 data drive, revised threshold, removal of the level shifter, and obsolete level-shifter attributes.

The standalone USB requirement defines its regulator, operating condition, and listed powered loads without assigning the LEDs to that path; message 444 does not establish a change to standalone USB power behavior.
Both 3.3V and 5V system rails remain required, and the AXP2101 remains the normal-operation power source; only the LED load moves between rails.
The LED supply change does not alter the configured 3.4V DCDC1 output, its 2A rating, the downstream 3.3V target, or the Schottky-drop compensation rule.
The LED rail change does not affect the panel button connector, its PWRON signal connection, location, or switching behavior.
Message 444 changes LED electrical operation but does not modify ESP32 clocking, sleep policy, deep-sleep conditions, or wake sources.
The LED supply decision has no necessary effect on the battery connector family, pin count, pin functions, compatibility, or unresolved physical pin order.
Moving the LEDs from 5V to 3.3V does not change the specified battery overcharge, overdischarge, or thermal-protection behavior.
The current charge-status requirement uses a separate future external LED through J_LED_CHG, not the SK6812 indicator supply path changed by message 444.
The LED supply and data-level decision does not alter the power-board TVS ESD protection requirement.
The interboard interface must still carry both 3.3V and 5V because the sensor board retains loads on both rails; message 444 does not change connector topology or pinout.
